accuracy.reason: Cards 1-5 correctly teach interaction roles, shared protocol/message semantics, local versus external session context, shared-service benefits/dependencies and uncertain request outcomes. RFC, Azure and MDN passages support the boundaries; no hardware, no-state or automatic-scale guarantees.

evidence.quote: Client and server describe roles. When a server calls another service, it acts as a client.

mechanisms.reason: Request/response actors, method-target-content-status, access checks, session placement and lost-response causes form traceable mechanisms. The learner applies them to allowed shared-data work, separating persistent data from session context.

evidence.quote: The server must check what each user can access. A hidden button does not prevent someone from sending a request.

coherence.reason: Programming/network prerequisites suffice; roles precede protocol, state, dependencies and request synthesis. Diagrams show exchange direction, optional server storage, local session dependency and client/server trade-offs. Stateful diagram is read with text explicitly limiting the issue to the only local copy.

evidence.quote: Stateless does not mean no stored data. Stateless servers can use a shared database.

decisions.reason: Cards 3-5 connect local versus shared state to routing/failure and local versus remote work to responsiveness, sync, latency and capacity. Retry is an application decision after uncertainty. Benefits and costs support an actual placement choice.

evidence.quote: Choose where each task runs based on its needs. Keep trusted checks on the server. Use the client for work that needs a fast response or must work offline.

clarity.reason: All five objectives use defined terms and direct prose; learner gaps concern optional application-specific details, not criteria. Shared renderer/CSS inspected previously and identical; diagrams inspected for meaning, no browser execution claimed.

evidence.quote: Connect the request, responsibilities, data and outcome. Component names alone do not explain behavior.

outcomes.reason: Criteria 1-5 satisfied: learner defines roles independent of browser/hardware/location, server-as-client, shared protocol, HTTP request/response fields, and application payload/error meaning; slides 1-2 support the trace.

Criteria 1-6 satisfied: learner defines retained session context, local dependency, stateless request context/shared retrieval, replacement and shared-store failure, database/auth compatibility, central reuse and latency/overload/availability limits. Slides 3-4 support each consequence.

Criteria 1-3 satisfied: actual learner traces input/check/work/result, separately locates persistent/session data, and distinguishes explicit reported failure from response-loss uncertainty. Its illustrative placement follows slides 2-5; unspecified fields/retry rules are outside criteria.

sourceChecks.claim: Live RFC 9110 sections 3.3-3.5 explicitly define interaction roles and one program as both client/server; browser is only one user agent.
Live RFC 9110 core semantics and sections 3.4/6.2 describe method, target, fields, content and response status; application meaning and error outcomes are properly distinguished.

Live Azure autoscaling recommends stateless design without dependence on a particular instance or request affinity. External-state/session consequences follow this plus the stated separate-process prerequisite.

Live MDN describes server-side shared data/behavior and dynamic database-backed responses; Azure capacity guidance and RFC request exchange support network/capacity costs. No automatic availability is claimed.
Live RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 explicitly permits original success with lost response and constrains non-idempotent retry. Supports uncertainty and application retry decision.
